title: Settings tests race under Odin's default parallel test runner — ci-local gate 2 fails nondeterministically (~25% of runs)
evidence:
app/settings_test.odin:15-23:
settings_test_seq: u64 // package counter — unique within the test binary

tmp_settings_path :: proc(t: ^testing.T) -> string {
	settings_test_seq += 1
	...
	path := strings.concatenate({dir, "/pp-settings-test-", fmt.tprintf("%d", settings_test_seq)}, context.temp_allocator)
(comment at :13-14: "hermetic: parallel/CI runs never collide within a binary")

Reproduced run (odin test app -out:bin/app-test, default flags):
[INFO ] --- Starting test runner with 13 threads. Set with -define:ODIN_TEST_THREADS=n.
settings: no readable settings at /var/folders/.../pp-settings-test-8 — defaults   [printed 7x — seven tests collided on ONE path]
[ERROR] --- [settings_test.odin:126:settings_scale_out_of_range_defaults()] an out-of-range scale step must fall back to defaults
(an earlier run failed [settings_test.odin:93:settings_bad_checksum_defaults()] instead)

Empirical: 5/20 default-thread runs failed; 0/40 with -define:ODIN_TEST_THREADS=1.

tools/ci-local.sh gate 2 (this diff): "Core unit tests (the determinism + topology contracts)|mkdir -p bin && odin test core && odin test app -out:bin/app-test && odin test app/render -out:bin/render-test && odin test harness -out:bin/harness-test"
detail: Odin's test runner executes @(test) procs on a thread pool by default; the non-atomic package counter hands the same temp path to concurrent tests, whose fixture writes/removes interleave (a sibling's settings_save_at overwrites the poisoned fixture, so load returns non-defaults). The '10/10 CI' claim is luck, not green.
recommended_fix: Make tmp_settings_path concurrency-safe: derive the suffix from the test's identity (e.g. hash of t.name) or atomically increment settings_test_seq via core:sync; alternatively run the gate with -define:ODIN_TEST_THREADS=1.

title: Python bytecode cache tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc is committed and not gitignored
evidence:
diff hunk: "diff --git a/tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc b/tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc / new file mode 100644 / Binary files /dev/null and b/tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc differ"

$ git ls-files | grep -i pycache
tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc

.gitignore (post-diff) ends with: "*.dSM/\n.pp-settings.bin" — no __pycache__/ entry anywhere in the file.
detail: A build artifact/cache is tracked in the tree; it silently goes stale whenever tools/derive_a11y_palettes.py changes and pollutes every future diff. Project convention keeps caches out (bin/, .godot/, *.dSYM are all ignored).
recommended_fix: git rm --cached tools/__pycache__/derive_a11y_palettes.cpython-313.pyc and add a '__pycache__/' line to .gitignore in the same commit.

title: Crisis-outline reduced-motion pin bypasses pulse_read, duplicating the seam the PR claims is single-source
detail: Two independent reduced-motion gates that must stay in sync; behavior is identical today (both pin 1.0) but a future change to one (e.g. pinning to a mid-envelope value) silently misses the crisis outline.
recommended_fix: Route the outline's factor through pulse_read (crisis.odin consumes PULSE16 directly; pulse_read wraps pulse_factor — refactor or have crisis call pulse_read), or correct the single-seam claim.

title: step_of has no production caller — only its own unit test references it
detail: Dead helper outside tests; its documented consumer (the panel display) computes the percentage from snap.ui_scale directly, so the comment misleads and the proc is unshipped code.
recommended_fix: Delete step_of and its two test lines (settings_test.odin:135-136), or actually use it where the reverse read is needed.

title: PR body's settings-panel section still says '25/25 parity scenarios green' — the shipped count is 27
evidence:
_pr_body.md:50: "...identical (empty) command streams + identical end input-state. **25/25 parity scenarios green.**"

vs _pr_body.md:89 (r2→r3 section): "— 27 parity scenarios, all biting."

Code reality: $ grep -c 'name = "input_parity' harness/parity.odin → 27; live run: "PASS input-parity   27 scenario(s) green — mouse == touch == controller (ODN-12 / FORGE #6)"
detail: The unchanged top section of the tracked PR body contradicts the r3 section and the code; a reader auditing the top-level claims gets a stale count for the parity gate.
recommended_fix: Update the '25/25 parity scenarios green' line in _pr_body.md to 27/27 (or drop the count so it cannot go stale again).
